Well, I really think everything I've done in my life has helped me prepare to be governor. You're kind of a product of your past, whether it's growing up in small family business, being the county prosecutor or the other jobs I've held. This may sound like a strange thing to say considering what's on the news every night. We've got a contentious issue now that's going to be a tough lift, frankly, for people in the state legislature. And boy, I understand it. I served in the elective office while I was voting for 22 years. But that is what we're going to do with our gas problem, with our roads, our ODOT problem. We inherited a pretty significant problem. We have a deficit of about a billion and a half dollars every single year in regard to our highways. And people say, well, how did that just come up? Well, it didn't just come up, but it's sort of been hidden a little bit because the state had issued some bonds. and got a lot of money up front and that money was able to kind of carry us through for a few years. That money's now pretty much gone and now we're left with a structural deficit of about a billion and a half dollars a year. Now that impacts all of you because 40% of that money goes down to the townships. part of it goes down to the cities, the villages, and certainly into the county engineers.
